title: alnus glutinosa
intro: Alnus glutinosa, commonly known as Black Alder, is a deciduous tree species native to Europe and Western Asia, belonging to the Betulaceae family. The bark and leaves of Black Alder have been used in traditional medicine to treat various health issues, including fever, inflammation, and respiratory problems, due to its health benefits in reducing inflammation and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Black Alder include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, which contribute to its use in treating conditions such as bronchitis, coughs, and sore throats. The bioactive constituents of Black Alder include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenes, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and have been studied for their potential in treating various diseases.
